strings.landing.worlds.label: One algorithm
strings.landing.worlds.title: Written once, evaluated in every world
strings.landing.worlds.body: Horner's rule needs only a semiring. The same function evaluates $1 + x^2$ over machine integers, floating point, big integers, complex numbers and matrices. It has no root among the integers, a root $i$ in the complex numbers, and a rotation as a root among matrices.
strings.landing.diagram.label: Structure-preserving maps
strings.landing.diagram.title: Structure travels with the map
strings.landing.diagram.body: A homomorphism proven once lifts to polynomials, matrices and products without a new proof. Two paths that must agree, agree: evaluate then map, or map then evaluate.
strings.landing.pillars.label: Principles
strings.landing.pillar1.title: Abstraction before implementation
strings.landing.pillar1.body: Begin from structures and laws. Implementation details stay inside the layer that needs them.
strings.landing.pillar2.title: Semantics made explicit
strings.landing.pillar2.body: Floating point, arbitrary precision and decimal values all add, but they do not mean the same thing. Luna Flow keeps the difference visible.
strings.landing.pillar3.title: Interoperability over isolation
strings.landing.pillar3.body: Independent libraries join through small traits and lightweight adapters, then compose into one computational world.
strings.landing.library.lead: Every repository documents its API, its design and a tutorial in the same structure, in English, Chinese and Japanese.
strings.landing.summary: Write the mathematics once. Choose the numbers later.
strings.landing.summary.lead: Algebraic traits describe what an algorithm needs. Number types decide what it means. Luna Flow keeps the two apart, so the choice stays yours.
strings.landing.precision.label: Numerical semantics
strings.landing.precision.title: Same equations. Two number systems.
strings.landing.precision.body: One Runge–Kutta integrator runs the Lorenz system twice from the same point, once in Float and once in Double. Rounding alone sends them apart. Luna Flow makes the number system an explicit choice.
